results.content: One key finding shows that a ZnFe2O4 /coffee ground residue biochar composite achieved 100% degradation of Methylene Blue (MB) dye in 60 minutes via a photo-Fenton process, showcasing the potential of sustainable, waste-derived materials for environmental remediation. Our analysis also covers: 🔹 Characterization of low-grade waste resources (LGWR) 🔹 Advances in bioleaching mechanisms and microbial strategies 🔹 SWOT analysis of bioleaching for LGWR 🔹 Market trends and industrial perspectives 🔹 A case study highlighting a waste in future supply chains 🔗 Full article available here: https://lnkd.in/eHbwKNMv 🙏 A heartfelt thank you to my supervisors and coauthors, Peter Ralph, Phong Vo, Sana Malik, for their constant support and invaluable insights throughout this research journey! 📢 In our latest article, published in Sustainability MDPI, titled: “𝐒𝐜𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐫𝐢𝐨-𝐁𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐱𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭–𝐁𝐞𝐧𝐞𝐟𝐢𝐭 𝐀𝐧𝐚𝐥𝐲𝐬𝐢𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐄-𝐖𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞 𝐌𝐞𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐑𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐢𝐧 𝐋𝐨𝐰-𝐈𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐬: 𝐄𝐯𝐢𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐟𝐫𝐨𝐦 𝐚𝐧 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐌𝐨𝐝𝐞𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐁𝐮𝐫𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐚 𝐅𝐚𝐬𝐨”, we applied a scenario-based Extended Cost–Benefit Analysis (ECBA) to model pathways for e-waste recovery, combining: ✔️ Technological selectivity ✔️ E-waste local collection cost variations ✔️ Policy incentives (EPR subsidies, eco-taxes) ✔️ Socio-environmental co-benefits (CO2 emission and pollution reduction, job creation).

results.title: Sustainability Roundtable — UofL Sustainability
results.content: ## UofL Sustainability. **Sustainability Roundtable**All UofL faculty, staff, and students and members of the broader public interested in research related to sustainability are encouraged to join us for an on-going series of Sustainability Roundtables. The purpose is to expand each other's horizons and to build capacity and connections for interdisciplinary sustainability research. We achieve this by gathering to share research interests, goals, and projects; hear from sustainability practitioners and those in government; have roundtable discussions about sustainability research; and discuss specific sustainability topics of common interest. Our Roundtables are open to those from all disciplines, practitioners, and the public at large. *We are excited to announce the reintroduction of the Sustainability Roundtable series and invite you to present. We welcome faculty, staff, community members, and Ph.D. students to present, and encourage a wide range of contributions, including: (1) recently completed research related to any aspect of sustainability; (2) ongoing research projects by faculty or graduate students; and (3) community-based sustainability projects and partnerships.
